blurb:
This place has become a regular lunch stop for me. It's not fancy and it doesn't try to be. It's a casual, no-fuss Middle Eastern spot where the food is genuinely good and the price won't make you think twice. Good for a quick weekday lunch, a low-key dinner, or grabbing takeout on the way home.

The shawarma is the move. It's what comes up in practically every review and for good reason. The falafel is solid too if you want to skip the meat. They have veggie-friendly options throughout the menu, which my wife appreciates when she's along for the ride. And don't skip dessert if anything in the case catches your eye.

Prices are very reasonable, which makes it easy to come back often. Ours has become a go-to for nights when we want something filling and different without any fuss.

blurb:
If you've lived in Marietta for more than five minutes, you already know about this place. The neon out front is basically a landmark at this point. It's open 24 hours a day, every single day, which means it's become the default answer for a long list of situations: late night after a game, big family breakfast on a Saturday, or just one of those Tuesday afternoons where you want a real meal and don't feel like cooking.

The menu is massive. Greek specialties show up alongside classic diner breakfasts and just about everything else you can think of. My wife loves the breakfast plates, and honestly it's hard to go wrong whatever time of day you land there. The portions are generous in a way that feels old school and intentional.

It gets busy, especially on weekends and late nights. Worth knowing going in, but it moves fast and the staff has seen everything. Don't let a crowd talk you out of it.

blurb:
This is the answer when your group can't agree on where to eat. Marietta Square Market is a food hall with about twenty different vendors under one roof, so everyone picks what they want and you all sit together. It's right off the Square, which makes it a natural stop before or after walking around the area. Good for families, good for friend groups, good for a casual weekday lunch.

Because there are so many vendors covering different cuisines, the honest recommendation is to walk the whole thing before you commit. See what's moving and what looks good that day. My wife and I have never left disappointed, and we've never ordered the same thing twice.

Friday and Saturday hours run until 10pm, which gives it a decent window for a relaxed evening out without feeling rushed.

blurb:
All-you-can-eat Brazilian barbecue in Marietta. Yeah. It's real and it's as good as it sounds. This is the spot I take people when they visit from out of town and want something memorable. It also works great for a group dinner where everyone has different tastes, because the spread covers a lot of ground.

The barbecue is the main event, but the cheese bread has its own fan club and for good reason. If you go on the weekend, they do breakfast starting at 7:30am, which is worth knowing. The feijoada stew shows up on the menu too for anyone looking to go deep into Brazilian comfort food.

Friday and Saturday they're open until 11pm, which gives you room for a late dinner without rushing. It's a relaxed place. The kind of meal that goes long in the best way.

blurb:
Nearly 21,000 reviews and a 4.9 rating. I don't throw that out there to pad a blurb. I bring it up because it's basically unheard of at that volume, and once you go, you understand why. This is a French bakery in Marietta that is legitimately the real deal. It's become our Saturday morning tradition and it earns that spot every single week.

The baguettes are exactly what you want a baguette to be. The quiches are what my wife reaches for first. The petits fours are worth grabbing on the way out if anything is left in the case, which is not a guarantee. Get there early if you want the best selection.

They're open at 7am Monday through Saturday, which makes it a great first stop before the rest of your day gets moving. Sundays they open at 9am and close at 3:30pm, so plan accordingly if Sunday brunch is the goal.
